record.original_question: Given a finite block of digits a1...am in base b, determine whether there exist prime numbers whose base-b expansion contains that block, and ask the same existence question for the sequences n! and n^n.

evidence.quote: Let a1, a2, ..., am be digits. Are there primes, on a base b, which contain the group of digits a1 ... am into its writing? ... But n! ? But nn ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer base $b\ge 2$ and a finite block of digits $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_m$ with each $a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}$. Say that a positive integer $N$ "contains" the block $a_1\ldots a_m$ if the string $a_1a_2\cdots a_m$ appears as a (consecutive) substring of the base-$b$ representation of $N$.

(a) Determine whether, for every base $b$ and every finite digit block $a_1\ldots a_m$ in base $b$, there exists a prime number $p$ whose base-$b$ expansion contains the block $a_1\ldots a_m$.

(b) Determine whether, for every base $b$ and every finite digit block $a_1\ldots a_m$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that the base-$b$ expansion of $n!$ contains the block.

(c) Determine whether, for every base $b$ and every finite digit block $a_1\ldots a_m$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that the base-$b$ expansion of $n^n$ contains the block.
artifact.category_tag: digits of primes and special sequences
artifact.status_search_result: For primes the question can be settled affirmatively: any fixed digit block appears in the base-$b$ expansion of infinitely many primes (this follows from results on primes in arithmetic progressions, and is strengthened by recent work such as Maynard's theorem on primes with restricted digits and Vinogradov-type theorems for primes with prescribed digits). For $n!$ and $n^n$ the analogous statements do not appear to be established in the literature; results on the digits of $n!$ and $n^n$ remain very limited and the general containment problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Vinogradov's theorem for primes with restricted digits
status_evidence.snippet: For sufficiently large base g and digit b, every sufficiently large odd integer is a sum of three primes whose base-g expansions avoid the digit b.
status_evidence.claim: Strong results are known about the digits of primes, supporting that any digit block occurs among primes.

status_evidence.title: Digit expansions of numbers in different bases (Burrell, Yu)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies digit expansions of natural numbers in different bases.
status_evidence.claim: Digit-occurrence problems for special sequences are an active area, but n! and n^n cases are not settled.
